Successful primary authentication creates a five-minute browser-bound EMAIL_LOGIN transaction and delivers a cryptographically random six-digit code through explicit authenticated STARTTLS. No session exists until code completion; SMTP unavailability fails closed. Active runtimes require email verification for password and Google sign-in, including accounts with historical authenticator enrollment; they never fall back to password-only access. The HttpOnly browser correlation cookie lasts 15 minutes to allow a rate-limited resend after code expiry; the code itself remains valid for five minutes only. X-Bidora-Challenge-Expires-At reports the code deadline, not the cookie deadline.

An expired EMAIL_LOGIN code may be replaced for up to ten additional minutes while its browser correlation cookie, current identity/auth epoch, unconsumed state and attempt limits remain valid. Expired codes never verify. TOTP transactions cannot use email resend. The replacement cookie lasts 15 minutes; X-Bidora-Challenge-Expires-At reports the fresh five-minute code deadline.
